native_result.query: At what Socioeconomic levels is the advantage in completion rates for Black students more pronounced?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))
native_result.HypoB: The advantage in BA-degree completion rates for Black students is most pronounced at HIGH socioeconomic levels (top SES quintile/quartile). Unconditionally the Black–White completion gap narrows to near-parity at the top SES quintile (Black 3.45% = 7/203 vs White 3.53% = 50/1416; gap −0.08 pp, ratio 0.98) versus a gap of −1.08 pp (ratio 0.15) in the bottom quintile; the logistic SES×race interaction is positive and significant (interaction OR 1.59–1.69, p = 0.012–0.005), so the gap closes as SES rises. Conditioning on academic resources (ASVAB composite + class percentile) sharpens this: at average resources the conditional Black–White gap becomes positive above the SES median (+0.30 pp at p75, +0.90 pp at p95; +1.07 pp in the top quintile), so at high SES Black students complete BA degrees at higher rates than observationally comparable White peers.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded nls_ses_processed.csv (N=8773, no missing values, BA completion 2.69% overall). 2) Stratified gap analysis: exact BA-completion rates, Clopper-Pearson 95% CIs per race, Black−White and Black−nonBlack (White+Hispanic pooled) percentage-point gaps with score/Newcombe/Wald difference CIs, ratios, and per-stratum Fisher exact tests, across SES terciles/quartiles/quintiles/binary (quantile cutoffs on full analytic sample). 3) Interaction: logistic BA ~ SES_std*Black (White reference; +Hispanic-control variant) and discrete BA ~ C(quintile)*Black; reported interaction ORs, predicted gaps at SES percentiles with delta-method CIs, and top-vs-bottom quintile contrast. 4) Conditional sensitivity: refit with ASVAB_std + PCT_std (covariates at overall means) and per-quintile conditional Black log-ORs. 5) Decision rule: most-favorable stratum = least-negative pp gap / ratio closest to 1; significance flagged where weak (discrete k5-vs-k1 contrast p=0.174 due to sparse top-quintile Black cells; continuous interaction significant p≈0.012).
